newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian Moslem party sees no union with UMNO.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian Moslem party sees no union with UMNO.

text.p: The fundamentalist Moslem party controlling Malaysia's only opposition-run state said on Friday it could not work together politically with the dominant UMNO party since the groups had different goals.

Kelantan state's Chief Minister, Nik Aziz Nik Mat, said UMNO (United Malays National Organisation) focused on nationalism while his Parti Islam se-Malaysia (PAS) strove to uphold Islamic principles, the national Bernama news agency reported.

"If UMNO wants to accept Islamic policies, then there will be no problems between us. But as long as it pursues nationalistic policies, it has to carry on with its way and we have our own way too," he told reporters at his residence in northeastern Kelantan state on Friday.
He said ties between the two parties would be confined to collaboration in economic and social fields, as PAS would continue its role as an opposition party, Bernama reported.
PAS governed Kelantan in a coalition with the smaller Spirit of 46 opposition party until the latter decided to dissolve and join Mahathir's UMNO last October.
Spirit's desertion has left Nik Aziz with a fragile minority in the state assembly.

PAS, which has controlled Kelantan since 1990, has laid down measures to create a more Islamic society, including bans on gambling and amusement parks. It has also mandated separate supermarket lines for men and women and warned women against wearing too much make-up.
The stance is at odds with Mahathir's government, which calls for a more tolerant brand of Islam in multiracial Malaysia.
Mahathir has said he is open to forming a coalition government in Kelantan with PAS but that the rival party should not make too many demands of his government.
